column1: # Gloss-shift repairs for the NTU source JSONs. Read by gloss_shift.load_table and
# applied at load time by pipeline_{grammar,sentences,stories}.py -- the JSONs are
# never written. Only rows whose status is 'accepted' take effect; set
# NTU_GLOSS_SHIFT_STATUSES=accepted,proposed to trial the rest in a scratch build.
# record_sha256 pins the targeted record(s): a drifted source fails the build.
# i/j index rows of the targeted record(s), apparatus rows included. 'fill' is
# refused unless 'reviewer' is set. Proposals come from find_gloss_shifts.py.
# withdrawn (kept for the record, never applied).

column12: As proposed (window from runis) this gives runis=bare, ku=NOM but leaves kung='here'. kung is 1SG.NEU in 71% of its corpus uses, so the span most likely starts at kung (i=3: kung=bare, runis=here, ku=NOM); the detector prefers the shorter window because kung/here is attested once elsewhere. Needs a reader's call on i.
ragiax (mountain) is bare and 'mountain' sits on imu. Span start is uncertain: ku=in / nian=house may also be displaced (3 alternatives score).
al-an's gloss absorbed the separately written clitic niam (=1EPL.GEN), so niam took su's ACC and su took tumuk's 'chief'. Split at '=' restores all four.
The audit's test case: climb-LF=1SG.GEN belongs to rakiyas-an=mu, not ku. Span START is uncertain: source note says 'hani yaku' = turned out; review whether hani or yaku lost the gloss.
nukah-an's gloss absorbed the clitic sami (=1PL.NOM); sami=PN, papak=CONJ, ru bare. Split at '=' gives sami=1PL.NOM, papak=PN, ru=CONJ.
m<in>-ukahul's gloss absorbed the clitic sami (=1PL.NOM); sami=LOC and i bare. Split gives sami=1PL.NOM, i=LOC.

Not in the audit. The unintelligible X's gloss X/?? sits on la, and la's PART on ru. After: X=X/??, la=PART, ru bare. The builder drops a lone 'X' whose gloss only echoes it, so the published result is la=PART and ru bare; ru's own gloss (CONJ in 333 of 337 uses) was lost upstream. NTU's 2026-01-10 release has exactly X=X/??, la=PART, ru=CONJ.
Same sentence repeats 'kia ku ruma' ga' correctly glossed (EXIST NOM some TOP) in record 33; in record 31 ku's NOM is missing and some/TOP slid left.
su lost ACC; 'bear' slid onto su and ngarux (bear) is bare. Record 56's bare 'i' is a separate omission, not repaired.
nha' lost 3PL.NEU; LNK, <AF>harvest, TOP each slid one word left. After: k<um>loh=<AF>harvest (the <um> infix matches <AF>), ga=TOP.
i lost its gloss; AF-work and ACC slid left onto i and ma-tawwaw. After: ma-tawwaw=AF-work, sku=ACC.
